subject: IPMs - question on modelling the link between count and population size data

messages.author: 3e911bc3bc76c82d
messages.subject: IPMs - question on modelling the link between count and population size data
parts:
Hi all!

I have a question about IPM structures that is perhaps basic or has an evident answer. Sorry in advance if this is the case.

I've been reading and working with IPMs lately and my question is specifically about the observation equations that link the observed population counts (i.e. often census data) with the population sizes calculated within the model. That is, for instance, if a normal distribution is chosen to model this link:

Census[t] ~ dnorm(N[age1,t] + N[age2,t], sigma) 

where Census[t] are the yearly population counts and N[age,t] are the population size estimations made by the model for different age classes at every year.

or if we choose a poisson distribution:

Census[t] ~ dpois(N[age1,t] + N[age2,t])

All links I can remember to have read between both components of the IPM are calculated using either poisson or normal distributions. However, as I understand, both of these distributions are accounting for both imperfect detection (false negatives) and double counting (false positives).
 In the case of some study species (mine in this case), there might be different conditions. For instance, in territorial species with strong tenacity to breeding locations throughout their lives and rare-to-no breeding dispersal events, double-counting might be almost impossible or, if present, extremely rare, as individuals will remain in the same location throughout their lives. I am wondering if by using poisson or normal links between both processes in these types of species, we are providing a wrong picture of the uncertainty in the relationship between both processes in the IPM, which may affect the overall performance of the model. In the case that my premise is true, does anybody have an idea about how to deal with this scenario, perhaps by choosing alternative distributions or structures?

Thank you in advance and have a nice day!

Jaume A.

messages.author: 312eda23f89ab6c6
messages.subject: AW: IPMs - question on modelling the link between count and population size data
parts:
Hi Jaume,

First of all we have to see that the 'observation error' of the IPM is infact the residual error of the IPM, hence it accounts not only for errors in the counts, but also for lack of fit in other parts of the model. Ideally we should decompose the residual error into a component of true observation error and a component of lack of fit. However, with the usual sampling design with a single count each year this decomposition is not possible.
Having this in mind, it may make sense that the variation of the counts can be in both directions, even if the counts themself are only subject to imperfect detection. Since your counts only have the imperfect detection issue the binomial distribution seems a natural choice, but the detection parameter is not identifiable with a single count. Hence, the remaining options remain therefore the Normal and the Poisson, or the log-Normal. Keep in mind that the estimated population sizes are in this case relative and not absolute.

Best wishes

Michael
